candidates.text: Public members that are not XNA 4.0 API carry the EXT suffix but no CNAEXT marker, so CNA_STRICT_XNA_API does not flag them: Texture::GetFormatSizeEXT, Texture::GetBlockSizeSquaredEXT, GameWindow::getIsBorderlessEXTProperty and setIsBorderlessEXTProperty. CHECKLIST.md requires every member outside the XNA 4.0 surface to be marked.
candidates.evidence: modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture.hpp (public static GetBlockSizeSquaredEXT, GetFormatSizeEXT, unmarked); modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GameWindow.hpp (public getIsBorderlessEXTProperty/setIsBorderlessEXTProperty, unmarked); CHECKLIST.md (CNAEXT markers)

candidates.text: The strict XNA-purity compile check (cna_strict_xna_api_check and its WILL_FAIL leak twin) exercises only the Microsoft::Devices/Sensors surface; no automated check covers marker completeness or strict-mode purity of the graphics, content, input, audio or media surfaces.

candidates.section: Glossary of XNA and CNA Terms
candidates.text: The glossary states that GraphicsCapability MRT and occlusion-query false positives are confirmed. At TARGET the base IGraphicsRenderer::SupportsCapability default is still permissive for the original members and DIRECTX9 inherits it wholesale, but DIRECTX9 implements MRT (bounded by NumSimultaneousRTs) and occlusion queries; which renderer, if any, still reports a false positive was not re-established.

The experimental C API release gate reports 'Not ready'. At TARGET the single unmet criterion is 'No public C++ symbol is unaccounted for' (468 public symbols unmapped), not unclassified modules as the preface says; no CI job builds the C library.

candidates.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
candidates.text: No workflow evaluates a ModuleLinkClosure_* contract against a real link line: scripts/check_module_link_closure.py reads CMakeFiles/<target>.dir/link.txt and exits 77 (SKIP) without it; the only workflow that runs an unfiltered ctest (general-tests-ci.yml) configures with -G Ninja, and the Makefiles-default lanes (devices-tests, apple-ci, metal-macos-ci) never run these tests. Its OPENGLES3 configuration also registers neither the HEADLESS native-SDK-free nor the Vulkan closure gates.

probe_core's forbid pattern (libcna_(?!core|math)|libCNA_|libenet|libav|cna_renderer_) does not forbid libSDL3, and its comment still says SDL3 is an accepted private detail of Logger.cpp, whereas modules/core/CMakeLists.txt states core no longer includes or links SDL; an SDL link re-entering cna_core would pass the gate.

modularization/tools/check_include_reachability.py and check_header_self_containment.py hard-code the August 2026 module graph (14 framework modules, no platform/diagnostics/design/phone/inspector/content-pipeline/video-ffmpeg/c-api, a pre-curation renderer map) and are referenced by no CMake file, CTest registration, workflow or script; by reading, the reachability table cannot reach the platform module from runtime, graphics, input or audio sources that include CNA/Platform headers.
candidates.evidence: modularization/tools/check_include_reachability.py (PUBLIC, PRIVATE, FAMILY tables); check_header_self_containment.py; grep of cmake/, .github/workflows/, scripts/

candidates.section: The migration was checked as a no-loss transformation
candidates.text: metal-macos-ci.yml's push paths filter lists cmake/BackendLibraries.cmake, cmake/Examples.cmake and cmake/Tests/MetalTests.cmake, none of which exists, and omits modules/renderers/metal/CMakeLists.txt and modules/renderers/metal/examples/CMakeLists.txt, where the Metal tests are registered; a push that changes only Metal registration does not start the workflow (pull requests are unfiltered).
candidates.note: The three dead paths are already noted in fact sheet 02 (C3); the missing Metal CMake paths are the new part.

candidates.text: cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64.cmake falls back to the i686-w64-mingw32 compiler when the x86_64 one is absent but keeps CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR x86_64, so the persistent SDL install key (.sdl-prebuilt-Windows-x86_64) mislabels a 32-bit toolchain; its header comment still requires pre-built SDL on CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH although the vendored SDL is built for the target at configure time.
candidates.note: Consequence (reuse of a mismatched SDL install) is inferred, not observed.

candidates.text: In a MinGW-w64 cross tree CnaTests receives a CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR (a Wine wrapper) only when the default renderer is DIRECTX9, DIRECTX11 or DIRECTX12 or DIRECT2D is compiled in; for any other default (for example SDL_RENDERER) gtest discovery and CTest would try to execute the Windows binary on the Linux host.
candidates.note: By reading; depends on whether the host hands PE files to Wine via binfmt_misc.

candidates.section: The Ninja caveat: registered does not mean executed
candidates.text: The link-closure tests pass --build-dir ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR} while the probe targets are defined in CNA's own root directory; when CNA is added as a subproject with tests on, the checker looks for CMakeFiles/<probe>.dir/link.txt in the consumer's root and always skips.

The source-partition validator globs only *.cpp and *.mm and checks path prefixes: headers and C sources outside every module are not reported, and a translation unit in a subdirectory of a renderer family's src/ passes the check but is never compiled by the non-recursive cna_add_renderer glob.

No current gate compiles each public C++ header of the framework modules in isolation: ContractIsSdlFreeTests compiles all platform contract headers in one TU and CApiHeaderCompatibility covers only the C headers.

Android has no preset, workflow, CMake API-level check or test route; the only Android build project is the Devices demo (NDK 30.0.14904198, API 24, arm64-v8a) which forces tests and examples off, so an Android build is compile-only evidence.
No workflow configures CNA_BUILD_C_API=ON, so whether the 0.29.0 C API library builds and installs at TARGET is unverified; CApi_InstalledConsumer is registered in source only.

ResetElapsedTime() sets forceElapsedTimeToZero_ only when IsFixedTimeStep is false, so under the default fixed step it does nothing; XNA 4.0's ResetElapsedTime sets its flag in both modes (and resets running-slowly counters) and its Tick zeroes the elapsed time before branching, so a blocking load followed by ResetElapsedTime produces a catch-up burst (up to 29 updates) in CNA but not in XNA.

IsRunningSlowly uses an FNA-style lag counter (set at 5 accumulated extra steps, cleared at 0) that no test pins; XNA 4.0 uses a different rule (two multi-step ticks within 20 ticks, assigned before each Update), so behaviour can diverge tick by tick and no oracle comparison exists.
Game::ShowMissingRequirementMessage is declared virtual but nothing in CNA calls it; XNA 4.0's Game.Run offers NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException and NoAudioHardwareException to it before rethrowing.

candidates.section: Properties, and one that is deliberately not settable from outside
candidates.text: InactiveSleepTime is validated and stored but never applied; an inactive CNA game keeps its normal rate, whereas XNA 4.0's Tick sleeps for InactiveSleepTime while inactive.
candidates.note: Already recorded as a gap on development/internals/runtime/module.html#state.

candidates.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
candidates.text: GameComponent::Dispose(true) raises Disposed but does not remove the component from Game.Components; XNA 4.0's GameComponent.Dispose(true) removes it first, so XNA code that disposes a component to retire it leaves it updated and drawn in CNA.

candidates.section: GameComponent and DrawableGameComponent: the update/draw ordering contract
candidates.text: DrawableGameComponent loads content once in Initialize and never subscribes to the device service (OnDeviceCreated is dead code; no DeviceDisposing hook), unlike XNA 4.0 which reloads on DeviceCreated and unloads on DeviceDisposing and requires an IGraphicsDeviceService.
GraphicsDeviceManager::FindBestDevice, RankDevices and CanResetDevice are never called by the manager; overriding them has no effect on device selection.

candidates.section: Explicit disposal, destructor cleanup, and the gap between them
candidates.text: Game::Dispose(true) walks Components by index re-reading the count instead of a snapshot (XNA 4.0 copies to an array); a component whose Dispose removes itself or another component shifts later entries and the next component is skipped by that pass.

candidates.section: What happens when a frame runs long
candidates.text: The zero-first-update rule is applied only on the fixed-step path; in variable step the first update receives the interval since Run() seeded the counter, while the XNA values recorded in GameClockFirstUpdateTests' variable-step comment imply zero elapsed time for XNA's first two variable-step updates. The test asserts only the total-lag relation.

candidates.section: The timing loop, ported wholesale from FNA
candidates.text: On Emscripten an exception thrown by a frame is caught and logged, the loop ends without raising Exiting, and Run() returns normally, so the game's caller cannot observe the failure.

Vector2/3/4::Divide(v, s), operator/(v, s) and Matrix::Divide(m, s) divide each component by s, whereas XNA 4.0 multiplies by one reciprocal 1/s; Vector3::operator/= alone uses the reciprocal and its comment wrongly says Divide does too, so v / s, v /= s and XNA's v / s can differ in the last bit.
candidates.evidence: modules/math/src/Vector2.cpp, Vector3.cpp, Vector4.cpp, Matrix.cpp (Divide, operator/=); XNA 4.0 IL (Vector3::Divide, op_Division, Matrix.Divide)

candidates.text: Ray::Intersects(BoundingBox) returns no hit for a zero-direction ray whose origin is inside the box (XNA returns 0), uses a 2^-24 parallel threshold where XNA uses 1e-6, and divides where XNA multiplies by a reciprocal.
Ray::Intersects(BoundingSphere) treats only a strictly inside origin as a hit at 0 (XNA uses <=), so a ray starting exactly on the surface and pointing outward returns no hit in CNA and 0 in XNA.
BoundingSphere::Contains(Vector3) returns Intersects for a point exactly on the surface; XNA 4.0 returns Contains only for d^2 < r^2 and Disjoint otherwise (never Intersects).

BoundingSphere::Contains(BoundingSphere) tests d^2 <= (R - r)^2, which loses the sign of R - r, so a larger argument sphere enclosing this one is reported as Contains (e.g. radius 1 containing a concentric radius 5); XNA tests R - r >= d and answers Intersects. Ported from FNA.

BoundingFrustum::Intersects(BoundingBox) and Intersects(BoundingSphere) are Contains(...) != Disjoint, a conservative per-plane test that reports true for volumes beside a frustum edge or corner; XNA 4.0 uses an exact GJK query. BoundingBox/BoundingSphere::Intersects(frustum) and the engine-layer culling helpers inherit it.
candidates.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingFrustum.cpp (Intersects overloads, Contains); XNA 4.0 BoundingFrustum.Intersects(ref BoundingBox/ref BoundingSphere) with Gjk

candidates.text: BoundingFrustum::Intersects(Plane) classifies corners with Plane::IntersectsPoint, so a corner exactly on the plane counts as Intersecting; XNA counts a zero distance as Back, so a frustum touching a plane from behind is Back in XNA and Intersecting in CNA.

Ray::ToString and BoundingBox::ToString emit literal doubled braces ({{Min:... }}) copied from FNA's string concatenation; XNA formats the same text with string.Format, which yields single braces. BoundingBoxTest.ToStringMatchesFNAFormat pins the FNA form, contrary to the project's XNA-over-FNA rule.
candidates.evidence: modules/math/src/BoundingBox.cpp, Ray.cpp (ToString); modules/math/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/BoundingBoxTests.cpp; XNA 4.0 BoundingBox/Ray.ToString; FNA b355124 src/BoundingBox.cs

candidates.text: Math ToString numbers use std::ostringstream defaults (six significant digits, C++ global locale) while XNA formats with Single.ToString(CurrentCulture); only Matrix::ToString's outer format was measured against XNA.

The FloatHash used by Vector2/3/4, Matrix, Quaternion (and CurveKey) hashes raw float bits, so values that compare equal (+0.0f vs -0.0f components) get different hash codes; .NET Single.GetHashCode returns 0 for both zeros, keeping XNA's hashes consistent with Equals.
candidates.evidence: modules/math/src/Vector3.cpp (FloatHash, GetHashCode); Matrix.cpp; Quaternion.cpp; mscorlib IL Single::GetHashCode

candidates.text: Point declares operator+, -, * and / (component-wise, no divide-by-zero guard), which XNA 4.0's Point does not have, without the CNAEXT marker, so CNA_STRICT_XNA_API does not flag them.

candidates.section: Color is packed, named, and polymorphic
candidates.text: Color::FromNonPremultiplied(intcs r, g, b, a) computes r * a / 255 in 32-bit int; XNA multiplies in 64-bit long and clamps, so arguments whose product exceeds INT_MAX overflow (undefined behaviour) in CNA.

BoundingSphere::CreateFromBoundingBox computes (Min+Max)/2 and Distance(center, Max) where XNA computes Lerp(Min, Max, 0.5) and Distance(Min, Max)*0.5; last-bit agreement is unmeasured (the sphere oracle covers CreateFromPoints only).

MathHelper::SmoothStep/Hermite/CatmullRom (double, endpoint shortcuts) and the vector SmoothStep/Hermite (float Hermite basis) use different arithmetic from XNA's float Lerp(t^2(3-2t)) and Hermite forms; last-bit agreement is unmeasured and no oracle covers them.

GraphicsDeviceManager subscribes a lambda capturing raw this to GameWindow::ClientSizeChanged, discards the removal token and never unsubscribes (Dispose removes only services), so a manager destroyed or replaced while its game window lives leaves a dangling resize callback.
GraphicsDeviceManager::Dispose(bool) raises Disposed before setting disposed_, so a Disposed handler that disposes the manager again re-runs Dispose (and can recurse).
A PreparingDeviceSettings handler that sets the GraphicsDeviceInformation adapter to null causes a null dereference in applyToExistingRenderer (Reset(pp, *adapter)); no argument check exists.
Calling ApplyChanges from a PreparingDeviceSettings handler recurses: prefsChanged_ is cleared only at the end of the pass, so the nested call raises the event again.

GraphicsDevice::Reset rolls back only window application and SetVirtualResolution; an exception from UpdatePresentationFormatEXT, ApplyMultiSampleCount or SetSwapInterval leaves the new presentation parameters stored, render targets unbound and DeviceReset unraised after DeviceResetting.

DIRECTX9 throws std::runtime_error "not yet implemented" from SetContextRecoveryEnabled and SetStringMarkerEXT; GraphicsDevice::SetContextRecoveryEnabled stores the flag before forwarding, so the device flag changes even though the call throws.
Family-specific clear defects named by the source text (an EasyGL colour-hook/depth coupling, a D3D9 additional back-buffer-format gate) were not re-read at TARGET.
candidates.evidence: not read; see renderer clear implementations in modules/renderers/easygl and directx9

candidates.section: Vector positions are quantized before they reach a renderer
candidates.text: Sub-pixel sprite and glyph destinations reach only EasyGL, OPENGL4 and SOFTWARE; every other family inherits ISpriteBatchRenderer's default float Draw, which truncates toward zero to an integer Rectangle.
candidates.evidence: modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/IGraphicsRenderer.hpp (ISpriteBatchRenderer float Draw default); overrides only in easygl, opengl4, software

candidates.text: EasyGL: a full-back-buffer SpriteBatch draw before the frame's first 3D draw breaks that frame's 3D rendering (Task 933, root cause not isolated).
candidates.evidence: docs/migration-guide.md (still listed); modules/graphics/examples/fullscreen_spritebatch_then_3d_test.cpp registered as EasyGL_/Vulkan_FullscreenSpriteThen3D; plans/plan_vulkan.md VULKAN-400 reports no reproduction

candidates.section: Flush timing: sorting without draw-call coalescing
candidates.text: SpriteSortMode::Immediate on EasyGL and Vulkan still batches below the ISpriteBatchRenderer seam, so a texture rewritten between two Draw calls is rasterised with its final contents for every sprite of the batch (recorded in CNA as VULKAN-057).

SpriteFont/DrawString pixel tests are registered for EasyGL, SDL_RENDERER, VULKAN, SOFTWARE, OPENGL4 and DIRECTX11/12 parity and FREEDIRECT only; the remaining families rely on shared layout code without a text pixel test.

candidates.section: RenderTargetUsage: three values, more than three behaviors
candidates.text: PresentationParameters.RenderTargetUsage is stored, cloned and exposed but never consulted when SetRenderTargets returns to the back buffer.

candidates.section: RenderTargetUsage: three values, more than three behaviors
candidates.text: Vulkan multi-target render passes begin every colour attachment with LOAD_OP_CLEAR from an undefined layout (except split continuations), so a PreserveContents/PlatformContents target loses its contents when bound as part of an MRT set.

candidates.section: Two SetData paths, and why GetData can hide a failed upload
candidates.text: Canvas and FreeDirect texture renderers throw for any Texture2D mip level above 0.
HEADLESS validates and traces TextureCube uploads but stores nothing, so cube SetData throws NotSupportedException and cube content paths cannot be exercised on HEADLESS.
Disposing an untracked Texture2D/TextureCube value copy (for example by its destructor) raises GraphicsDevice.ResourceDestroyed although no ResourceCreated was raised for it.
DIRECTX9 writes D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY without checking D3DCAPS9::MaxAnisotropy and reports AnisotropicFiltering through the inherited default.
METAL throws NotSupportedException for non-default MaxMipLevel/MipMapLevelOfDetailBias, partial colour-write masks and a non-default MultiSampleMask.
SDL_GPU cannot honour BlendState.MultiSampleMask; SDL documents the sample-mask fields as reserved.
EasyGL on GLES/WebGL contexts without GL_NV_polygon_mode or WEBGL_polygon_mode refuses wireframe triangle draws.
CANVAS and FREEDIRECT never apply a scissor rectangle; SDL_RENDERER ignores ScissorTestEnable and always clips to the rectangle.

candidates.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
candidates.text: SpriteEffect never creates a MatrixTransform parameter: CacheEffectParameters() looks it up on an effect with no parameters, so matrixParam_ is null and OnApply() returns before computing XNA's orthographic projection with half-pixel offset. XNA 4.0's SpriteEffect exposes MatrixTransform. Sprite projection is supplied by each renderer's SpriteBatch path, so ordinary drawing is unaffected; Parameters["MatrixTransform"] returns null.
candidates.bible_ref: Bible audit graphics-core-effects E6 (no CNA-BUG id)
candidates.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/SpriteEffect.cpp (CacheEffectParameters, OnApply); XNA 4.0 IL of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics SpriteEffect ctor (ldstr "MatrixTransform"); tests/SpriteEffectTests.cpp covers only Clone/Apply

candidates.section: Stock parameters are not compiled-effect reflection
candidates.text: Only BasicEffect exposes XNA's authentic parameter graph and technique name. AlphaTestEffect (no Texture), DualTextureEffect (no Texture/Texture2), EnvironmentMapEffect (no Texture/EnvironmentMap/DirLight*), SkinnedEffect (no Texture/DirLight*) expose partial hand-built tables and a 'Default' technique where XNA's compiled effects name the technique after the effect ('SpriteBatch' for SpriteEffect); EnvironmentMap/Skinned declare WorldInverseTranspose 4x4 where XNA's .fx declares float3x3, and Bones as 72x4 rows instead of float4x3[72].
candidates.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/{AlphaTest,DualTexture,EnvironmentMap,Skinned}Effect.cpp (CacheEffectParameters); BasicEffect.cpp (Effect(device,"BasicEffect")); XNA IL CacheEffectParameters strings; modules/renderers/fna3d/effects/*.fxb technique strings; modules/renderers/directx9/src/shaders/xna/{EnvironmentMap,Skinned}Effect.fx

candidates.section: Object lifetime, submission, and cloning are deliberately narrow
candidates.text: ShaderEffect::Clone() does not reject a disposed source (it rebuilds from the retained source strings), while every stock effect and compiled Effect::Clone() throws ObjectDisposedException for a disposed source since SOFTWARE-259.

DIRECTX9 inherits CustomEffects=true and declares neither a shader dialect nor ExecutesShaderEffectSourceEXT, so the capability profile states that ShaderEffect source does not determine pixels, yet D3D9EffectRenderer compiles caller HLSL (SM2/SM3) and D3D9SpriteBatch executes it; no DIRECTX9 3D draw consumes a custom program.

VULKAN and SDL_GPU report all six ShaderDialect* RendererFeature entries Unsupported because their declared dialect SpirV has no feature entry, although both execute caller SPIR-V; only SupportsShaderLanguageEXT(SpirV, stage) answers truthfully.
The engine layer's capability-name table used in refusal messages lists 18 of the 19 GraphicsCapability members; IndirectDraw is missing, so a refusal on it prints an unrecognised capability name.

candidates.section: GpuDrawParams: the shared stock-effect draw packet
candidates.text: GpuDrawParams::specularEnabled (EnvironmentMapEffect's XNA shader-variant switch, true for a non-black specular colour) is filled but read by no renderer, so a specular colour that is black-but-enabled cannot be distinguished from disabled specular.
METAL refuses ShaderEffect construction (NotSupportedException) and custom-effect 3D draws 'until the adapted renderer has passing macOS shader evidence'; the family cannot be built on Linux CI.

Stock-effect state is captured at draw time: GraphicsDevice calls currentEffect_->FillGpuDrawParams() inside each draw, so a stock-effect property changed after EffectPass::Apply() and before the draw affects that draw, whereas XNA uploads effect state at Apply(). Compiled effects synchronise at Apply() like XNA. Derived from reading; no test pins either behaviour.

CNA-constructed (stock/standalone) EffectParameter records are lenient: SetValue(string) is accepted on non-string records, SetValue(Texture*) fills a generic slot that GetValueTexture2D() does not read, and class/type/shape metadata is not enforced; no focused test covers these lenient-mode paths (compiled-mode type checks are exercised in EffectTests.cpp and CompiledEffectConformance.hpp).

GameWindow keeps the borrowed IPlatformWindow* it received in the Game constructor after the game explicitly disposes the GraphicsDevice (which destroys that window); nothing rebinds or clears it, so later GameWindow property calls can reach a destroyed platform window.

ShaderEffect::SetTexture(int, TextureCube&) and SetTexture(int, Texture3D&) pass texture.GetRenderer(), which dereferences a null renderer handle when the renderer's cube or volume factory returned null.

SDL_RENDERER applies any non-empty ScissorRectangle as its SDL clip rectangle regardless of RasterizerState.ScissorTestEnable (it has no ApplyRasterizerState override), so a game that sets a scissor rectangle with the test disabled is still clipped.

The WindowId-to-renderer registry has no ownership check or synchronisation: two devices attached to one borrowed window overwrite each other's entry and destroying one removes the other's; no test covers duplicate attachment, constructor failure after registration or concurrent lookup.
TextInputEXT and Mouse window slots are process-wide with last-writer semantics, so two live GraphicsDevices replace each other's input target; the multi-device lifecycle is untested.
No test on any family times PresentInterval::Two (half-refresh) against ordinary vsync; the registered interval tests check storage, forwarding and survival only.

FREEDIRECT stores the presentation mode but the wrapped free-direct presenter hard-codes letterbox; Stretch, Overscan and NativeBackBuffer cannot reach physical output. CANVAS changes output only for FixedHeightDynamicWidth and DIRECTX9 has no presentation-geometry override.
CANVAS and FREEDIRECT override neither SetViewport nor SetScissorRect, so GraphicsDevice.Viewport and ScissorRectangle have no effect on those 2D renderers.

DIRECTX9 inherits the default true AnisotropicFiltering answer and forwards the requested MaxAnisotropy to D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY without clamping to the device's MaxAnisotropy cap in ApplySamplerState (the compiled-effect path does consult caps).
METAL refuses back-buffer readback outright (disabled after a historical macOS run returned clear-colour-only data); GetBackBufferData throws NotSupportedException there.

EasyGL volume textures are not registered with the GL context-loss recovery registry (EasyGLTexture3DRenderer is not a RecoverableResource), so Texture3D content is lost after a real WebGL context loss; cube textures are registered.

EasyGL_GraphicsDevice_ReferenceStencil is still annotated in CMake as a documented known failure while EasyGLRenderer::SetReferenceStencil now re-issues the stencil function; whether the test passes at 009d40f5 is not established.
On OpenGL ES 3.0 and WebGL 2 contexts OcclusionQuery::PixelCount() is boolean (0 or 1) because only GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED exists; PixelCountIsPreciseEXT() reports it.
The WebGL identities (WEBGL1, WEBGL2) have no native test registrations; browser behaviour (context loss, presentation, host-owned loop) needs a separate browser run.

candidates.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
candidates.text: Vulkan occlusion queries record only the first contiguous run of tagged draws per frame; draws after a render-pass boundary inside one Begin/End span are not summed.

candidates.section: OcclusionQuery: current contract and render-pass limit
candidates.text: On VULKAN only 3D draws are tagged with the active OcclusionQuery; SpriteBatch draws between Begin and End do not contribute to PixelCount.
An enabled zero-area ScissorRectangle draws unclipped on VULKAN and SDL_GPU (expanded to the full target) but clips everything on WEBGPU and suppresses the draw on METAL.

candidates.section: SwapInterval to VkPresentModeKHR: the same three-way switch Chapter ch:game-loop introduced
candidates.text: No test times the real cadence of Vulkan present modes; FIFO_RELAXED late-frame behaviour is the specification's contract only.

candidates.section: METAL: a narrow implementation with explicit refusals
candidates.text: METAL refuses MRT, MSAA, custom effects, occlusion queries, instancing, multi-stream input and back-buffer readback.

candidates.section: METAL: a narrow implementation with explicit refusals
candidates.text: METAL's CI lane proves construction, clear/present and capability reporting but no representative 3D pixels.

candidates.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
candidates.text: WebGPU's back buffer always has a Depth24PlusStencil8 attachment but PresentationParameters keeps the requested DepthFormat (no applied-format override), unlike Vulkan's VULKAN-348 write-back.

candidates.section: Verification methodology, and how it differs from D3D9's
candidates.text: WEBGPU is selected by no CI workflow; native evidence is Linux x86_64 only and browser evidence is scripted headless Chrome.

candidates.section: The .cnj fixture exposes the remaining shader-compatibility boundary
candidates.text: The shared .cnj GLSL ES 3.00 effect fixture is not accepted by SDL_GPU's Vulkan-rule GLSL route; custom GLSL effects must use #version 450 with explicit locations and SDL_gpu sets.

candidates.section: The .cnj fixture exposes the remaining shader-compatibility boundary
candidates.text: CnjEffectTest.LoadsRealCnjFixture expects a valid effect on a renderer that reports CustomEffects, executes source and declares a non-HLSL dialect; under SDL_GPU with libshaderc that expectation conflicts with the renderer's rejection of GLSL ES 3.00 (not executed; whether CnaTests is run under SDL_GPU is not established).
SDL_gpu 3.5.0 exposes no occlusion-query commands, so SDL_GPU refuses OcclusionQuery creation.
SDL_GPU's Direct3D 12 and Metal driver routes have no native execution evidence (Direct3D 12 only via Wine/vkd3d-proton; Metal none); no workflow selects SDL_GPU.

candidates.section: SkinnedEffect's storage-buffer workaround and push-uniform limit
candidates.text: SDL_gpu's pushed-uniform limit (about 4,096 bytes measured on the Vulkan driver) forces SkinnedEffect's 4,608-byte palette into a texture.

candidates.section: One PresentInterval::Two, two opposite Direct3D mistakes
candidates.text: DIRECTX9 requests D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO without checking D3DCAPS9::PresentationIntervals or windowed mode; Reset can fail and retry every Present while public PresentationParameters keeps Two.

candidates.section: The public presentation-mode call reaches D3D11 and D3D12, but neither scales yet
candidates.text: DIRECTX9 stores PresentationMode and the virtual resolution but never reads them; every mode behaves like NativeBackBuffer.

candidates.section: MRT finalization across all bound targets
candidates.text: DIRECTX9 does not track an MRT set for finalisation: SetRenderTargets binds multisample surfaces of several targets but only a single tracked target is StretchRect-resolved on the next transition, so MSAA MRT targets may be sampled unresolved.
candidates.evidence: modules/renderers/directx9/src/DirectX9Renderer.cpp (SetRenderTargets comment 'MRT binds are NOT tracked'); D3D9RenderTargets.cpp (ResolveForTransitionEXT)

candidates.text: DIRECTX9 BasicEffect reaches only 12 of 32 variants; combinations without a matching CNA vertex layout throw 'no matching CNA vertex layout'; untextured VSBasicPixelLighting is permanently unproven.
DIRECTX9 RenderTarget2D ignores mipMap (single level; GetData level>0 throws NotSupportedException) and cube render targets ignore the MSAA request.
DIRECTX9 has no ClassifySurfaceFormatEXT, so public textures are Color-only although an internal D3DFORMAT mapping exists.
DIRECTX9 MultiSampleAntiAliasing and AnisotropicFiltering capability answers are unconditional defaults; D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY is set unclamped by ApplySamplerState.
DIRECTX9 SetContextRecoveryEnabled throws after GraphicsDevice already stored the new flag (partial state change of the Texture2D shadow policy).

candidates.section: One public ShaderEffect API, two Direct3D contracts
candidates.text: DIRECTX9's draw dispatch has no branch for a custom ShaderEffect; only SpriteBatch consumes a D3D9 ShaderEffect.

candidates.section: Only D3D9 consumes the presentation format/fullscreen hook
candidates.text: DIRECTX11/DIRECTX12 never enter DXGI exclusive full screen (no SetFullscreenState; exclusiveFullscreen_ always false).

candidates.section: One PresentInterval::Two, two opposite Direct3D mistakes
candidates.text: No test measures PresentInterval::Two pacing or the no-vsync tearing branch on any Direct3D renderer; genuine DXGI device removal is never triggered; DIRECTX9 has no CI job and native-Windows runs are manual.

candidates.section: MRT finalization across all bound targets
candidates.text: MRT combined with mipMap=true on the DXGI renderers is wired through the same finalisation helper but no fixture combining them was identified.
No in-progress marker in Load<T>: a self-referencing XNB chain (EffectMaterial effect reference, untyped external references) recurses until stack exhaustion.
A loose reader that re-registers its own T during Read destroys the executing reader object (Load<T> holds a reference into typeReaders_).
Loading .cnb from an Android packaged asset is not established: the CNB tiers use std::filesystem, not the platform loader.
LZX decode compares the produced length with the declared size only after the last block; output is not capped while decoding.
The object-nesting depth guard covers only typed InnerReadObject<T>; InnerReadObjectAny (Tag values, Dictionary<String,Object> values, shared resources) is unbounded.
No externally produced XNB fixture for Texture3D, Curve, Video, DXT1/DXT5 Texture2D, version-4 textures or four of the five stock effects.
CNJ documents have no size limit (read whole) and no fuzzer.
Vendored cgltf misaligned sparse-accessor read listed by CNA as a LOW accepted residual (REMED-CONTENT-010).
No CNJ document fuzzer; fuzzing covers the XNB container, LZX, the XNB writers and the CNB container only.

candidates.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
candidates.text: ModelMesh::Draw guards Ensure3DSupported with a null-device check but then dereferences graphicsDevice_ unconditionally for a positive-count part, so a mesh built with a null device crashes instead of failing cleanly.

candidates.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
candidates.text: Model::Draw on a zero-bone model with a mesh effect reads sharedDrawBoneMatrices_[0] without growing the vector (empty on a fresh thread, or a stale slot from an earlier model); operator[] is unchecked.
Only EasyGL has renderer-local Model draw/hierarchy example programs; other GPU families render Model graphs only through the glTF L7 campaigns.

candidates.section: A two-target morph from the test suite
candidates.text: BlendMorphTargetsEXT indexes NormalDeltas[t] for every weighted target without checking the outer vector length (TangentDeltas is guarded) and indexes non-empty inner delta vectors by vertex without a length check; hand-built MorphTargetDataEXT with short arrays is undefined behaviour.

candidates.section: Four model asset routes, not two
candidates.text: The .cnj and .cnb Model routes carry no imported cameras; only direct glTF fills Model::CamerasEXT.
asset.version is checked only when present and asset.minVersion is never inspected.
Runtime glTF import has no unit-scale control (fixed 1.0); only cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj and cna_tool_gltf_to_cnb scale; cna-content has no option.
EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing imports one placement per node and drops per-instance transforms (reported).
Mirrored (negative-determinant) placements are not winding-corrected and can disappear under default culling; reported per placement (mirrored-winding-unapplied).

candidates.section: Hard limits carried by the bytes
candidates.text: The vertex ABI carries at most two distinct UV sets, four joint influences and one colour set; the rest is dropped and reported.

AnimationPlayer sizes its vectors from static_cast<size_t>(BoneCount) before RecomputeTransforms validates, so negative BoneCount in hand-built SkinningData produces an allocation failure instead of ArgumentException.
A skinned model cannot carry rigid scene-node clips; rigid tracks not carried by a skin are dropped with the rigid-animation-dropped-on-skinned-model diagnostic.
Morph weight tracks come from the first node in file order that instances the mesh; every placement of a multi-placed mesh plays that track.
Cubic bone channels are baked onto union key times and played back linearly between them.
glTF skins with more than 72 joints are refused at import (palette limit).
The .cnj Model reader silently skips a mesh entry whose vertexStride is zero or negative instead of refusing the descriptor.
.cnj vertex/index sidecar sizes that are not whole multiples of the stride or index size are truncated by integer division rather than rejected.
The .cnj bones parser accepts a forward parent (parent >= child) and turns a transform of the wrong length into identity, loading an inconsistent graph instead of failing.
No native point/spot lights: glTF punctual lights are approximated as up to three directional lights (GLTF ROBUST row 6).
METAL samples neither KHR_materials_specular texture map (factor-only).
Whole-corpus L7 campaigns for VULKAN, SOFTWARE and DIRECTX11 are recorded reports (2026-08-18, CNA b6c180fd), not CI-run; only the OPENGLES3 L7 rung runs in CI through an external pinned viewer.
The bounded Khronos retake matrix qualifies three renderers; a fourth (GLTF ROBUST row 12) is pending.

candidates.section: Logical coordinates are a renderer contract
candidates.text: DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12 and FREEDIRECT implement TransformWindowToLogical/TransformLogicalToWindow but never call IGraphicsRenderer::RegisterForWindow, so Mouse, SetPosition and touch pass window coordinates through unchanged under a virtual resolution.

candidates.section: Logical coordinates are a renderer contract
candidates.text: On renderers whose TransformWindowToLogical returns false in a letterbox bar (EasyGL identities, OPENGL4, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, SVG_DOM, HTML_DOM), Mouse::GetState and the bridge report the raw window coordinate instead of an out-of-range logical one.

Mouse::GetGlobalPositionEXT, WarpGlobalEXT and SetCaptureEXT do not catch PlatformNotSupportedException, which the native Wayland and terminal mouse services throw, contradicting Mouse.cpp's comment that a platform without a desktop pointer answers (0, 0).
F9/F10 unconditionally trigger the renderer's context-loss debug seam in Game::PollEvents in every build; games cannot suppress it.
OemBackslash (the ISO 102nd key), VolumeMute and 38 other Keys have no scancode mapping, so the scancode/name helpers return None or empty for them.
WindowFocusLostDoesNotClearHeldKeysMatchingFna checks only the bridge's legacy accumulator; public keyboard snapshot behaviour across focus loss is not tested per platform.
Fifteen manual-hardware input checks remain blocked; joystick, host sensor, power, gamepad-extension and IME behaviour are unverified on real hardware.
Wayland gives clients no desktop pointer coordinates; browsers hide gamepads until a button press and gate pointer lock on a user gesture.

SoundBank::SweepFireAndForget destroys a fire-and-forget PlayCue cue that is still playing five minutes after it started (kFireAndForgetSafetyNet), cutting off long looping cues; XNA has no such limit.
DynamicSoundEffectInstance::SubmitBuffer/SubmitFloatBufferEXT do not validate frame alignment (XNA throws for a size that is not a whole number of frames).
Microphone::Start sets Started even when the device cannot be opened (FNA parity), so failures are invisible to callers.
XACT REPLACE_QUIETEST and QUEUE behave as REPLACE_OLDEST; cue-level victim search spans the whole bank (FAudio parity).
XACT per-track band-pass filters are unreachable from parsed content; reverb sends and DSP-preset RPC targets are no-ops.
InstancePlayLimitException is declared but never thrown.
XACT wave-bank entries in XMA/XMA2 or WMA produce no sound (stderr diagnostic only).
The three user-reported audio release blockers in plans/plan_audio.md are unchecked; no capture of the original game has been compared.

An intermittent late audio-filter test failure and an order-dependent teardown failure (Cue/DynamicSoundEffectInstance suites) were recorded against an earlier revision; not confirmed or ruled out at TARGET.
Whether the pinned SDL3_mixer keeps a built-in MIDI decoder is unestablished; docs/audio.html states MIDI is unavailable.
DynamicSoundEffectInstance pending-count units under resampling are not established by tests (same-format fixtures only).
In mixer-less builds (SDL2, NULL audio) MediaPlayer never auto-advances or ends a song, because queued copies have no duration.
The visualization failed-tap-installation branch is untested (media tests always have a mixer).
No video decoding on Windows, Emscripten, Android or iOS (FFmpeg backend never built).

Accelerometer, Gyroscope, Compass and Motion declare Dispose(bool) public; an external Dispose(false) marks the sensor disposed without stopping it, decrementing the instance count or releasing its platform lease.
The Android landscape remap is a reflection (determinant -1), not a rotation; CNA's own source flags it as an unresolved finding and it is not hardware-verified.
No hardware QA report exists; Android compass/motion sign conventions unverified on devices; Android demo is a stale copy.
VibrateController::StartLeftRight plays nothing (no fallback) on a device without a left/right haptic effect.
Compass and Motion exist only on Android; desktop sensors only through the SDL3 platform; web targets refused by policy.
SDL3 dialog and tray trampolines call caller-supplied C++ callbacks from SDL C callbacks without try/catch; a throwing handler unwinds across a C boundary.
CNA::Devices::PowerInfo reads the platform power info separately for each property, so state, percentage and seconds can come from different instants.
MessageBox dialogs are never parented and have no default/cancel button; SystemTray has no icon-image API; UrlLauncher does no validation.
CNA::Devices tests exercise canned platforms only; real dialogs, trays, cameras and permissions are unverified, and a default build compiles no devices-ext tests.

GamerPresence's 60-entry presenceModeStrings_ table is ordered alphabetically by mode name, but setPresenceModeProperty indexes it by the GamerPresenceMode ordinal (None=0 maps to 'Arcade Mode'); the selected string is currently unobservable (private, passed only to the empty SetPresenceModeStringEXT). Whether FNA shares the ordering was not checked.

Achievement earnedTicks, leaderboard ratings and int64 columns are stored as JSON doubles and lose low bits above 2^53 (2026 ticks rounded to 128-tick steps), while LocalGamerServicesStore.hpp documents earned ticks as an exact round trip.
The synchronous LeaderboardReader::Read/PageDown/PageUp wrappers never delete the action their Begin* allocates, unlike GetProfile/GetAchievements, leaking one small object per call.
Fourteen Guide Show* entry points plus DelayNotifications are empty no-ops (no local shell UI for sign-in, friends, marketplace, messages, party, gamer card, achievements).
Achievement catalogue metadata (name, description, gamer score) is never populated and Achievement::GetPicture() throws NotImplementedException.
Presence is never published (empty SetPresenceModeStringEXT) and GamerPrivileges is a fixed permissive constant that nothing enforces; GamerProfile is synthetic except Region.
StorageContainer::OpenFile discards its FileShare argument; FileStream has no share mode and no cross-process lock, so FileShare::None does not exclude other writers.
No C++ storage test writes bytes through a StorageContainer stream and reads them back; only the C ABI smoke test (C ABI builds only) does.
StorageContainer methods keep working after Dispose (no disposed check); XNA's behaviour after disposal was not checked here.
Under Emscripten no persistent filesystem is mounted (no IDBFS/syncfs in the tree), so storage and the GamerServices store are lost on page reload.
candidates.evidence: grep of TARGET tree (excluding third_party/vendor) for IDBFS|syncfs|FS.mount: no hits

candidates.text: Local and LocalWithLeaderboards sessions deliver no packets at all, not even between local gamers; PlayerMatch/Ranked/JoinInvited are refused.
LocalNetworkGamer::ReceiveData(PacketReader&, NetworkGamer*&) always returns 0 (preserved FNA quirk).

ReceiveData(PacketReader&) writes the packet at position 0 of the reader's stream without truncating it, so reusing one PacketReader for a shorter packet after a longer one appears to leave stale trailing bytes and an old Length (depends on sharp-runtime MemoryStream::Write, read at a sibling revision).
candidates.evidence: modules/net/src/Xna/LocalNetworkGamer.cpp (ReceiveData PacketReader overload); sharp-runtime (sibling, not pinned) MemoryStream::Write

candidates.text: NetworkSessionAction reports CompletedSynchronously == false although it is completed before Begin* returns.
A joining machine's session is constructed with MaxSupportedGamers (31) and four private slots (FNA FIXME placeholders), so a client's MaxGamers/PrivateGamerSlots do not mirror the host's.
Voice (EnableSendVoice, SendPartyInvites), NetworkMachine::RemoveFromSession, arbitration/TrueSkill events and QualityOfService bandwidth are unimplemented.
On Emscripten, LAN discovery is a no-op, hosting is only meaningful for a Node.js relay (fixed port 61191), and Join returns before the handshake.

Process-spawning transport and dispatcher tests are compiled out on Windows, Emscripten, Android and iOS; multi-machine discovery/migration, Windows shared-port binding and browser paths have no test evidence.
The bundled procedural avatar's garment shells interpenetrate the body (collar and cuffs visible; shirt 64/228 vertices crossing), per CNA's own record; four remedies were measured and reverted.

Avatar rendering evidence is three pixel programs on EasyGL and Vulkan using a synthetic one-bone quad; no renderer test validates the bundled 19-bone content, and no other renderer registers the programs.
SkinnedModelEXT::AttachPartEXT only checks BoneCount equality; a different skeleton with the same bone count is not detected.

candidates.section: The linking helper makes closures explicit
candidates.text: On Windows targets CNA leaves the sharp-runtime Xml.Serialization component out of its closure (CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_HAS_XML_SERIALIZATION OFF) and removes the math and input XmlSerializationEXTTests, so the XmlSerializationEXT surface is absent from Windows builds. The stated reason (Diagnostics' Process.cpp including <poll.h> outside its POSIX guard) was fixed in sharp-runtime next by 88c12f15 (2026-09-14), which next @ 41b918c9 contains; the CNA comment asks to remove the condition once that happens.

CNA records no sharp-runtime revision: the build adds whatever checkout sits at CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT, CI clones branches through scripts/ci/clone_siblings.sh, and several workflows pin August 2026 sharp-runtime commits (bc8dbf41, f23ded28, df1b42ab) that lack the Resources and Xml.Serialization components CNA's closure names, so those lanes should stop at configure with 'Unknown Sharp Runtime component'.
candidates.evidence: CMakeLists.txt (CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT); scripts/ci/clone_siblings.sh; .github/workflows/devices-tests.yml, htmldom-ci.yml, emscripten-multi-renderer-ci.yml, apple-ci.yml, metal-macos-ci.yml, content-pipeline-windows-ci.yml (sharp-runtime ref); sharp-runtime cmake/SharpRuntimeComponents.cmake (unknown component FATAL_ERROR)

candidates.text: CNA public headers Viewport.hpp, ContentManager.hpp and the Microsoft::Devices::Sensors reading headers include SharpRuntime/Prop.hpp, which defines 31 unnamespaced macros including YES, NO, nothing, ref1, static0 and getter1; SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp adds CONTAINS and INTERNAL. Any game translation unit including those headers has identifiers with those spellings rewritten by the preprocessor.

candidates.section: String and StringBuilder: static utility versus mutable buffer
candidates.text: sharp-runtime's text APIs (String, StringBuilder, Encoding counts) index and count UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units (declared permanent deviation #2015); positions and lengths differ from .NET for non-ASCII text and byte-range edits can leave ill-formed UTF-8.

candidates.section: Generic continuations exist; generic combinators do not
candidates.text: Task::WhenAll and Task::WhenAny accept only std::vector<Task>; there is no overload for std::vector<TaskT<TResult>> producing a result array or a typed winner.

sharp-runtime tasks start one std::async thread per task (no pool) and throw PlatformNotSupportedException in single-threaded Emscripten builds; threaded web builds need SHARP_RUNTIME_ENABLE_EMSCRIPTEN_THREADS (set by CNA_ENABLE_EMSCRIPTEN_THREADS).

sharp-runtime's Regex is a header-only wrapper over std::regex with the ECMAScript grammar: .NET-only syntax is translated or stripped and match timeouts cannot interrupt a running search; the component has no component test executable (integration parity tests only).

candidates.section: The measured gate is not green
candidates.text: sharp-runtime's last recorded full gate before next @ 41b918c9 (NEXT.md, 2026-09-19) lists five failing Xml.Linq namespace tests, and its CI runs only on Ubuntu; Windows, macOS and Emscripten evidence is compile-only or downstream.

candidates.section: The executable boundary tests the dependency boundary
candidates.text: Four sharp-runtime module directories own no component tests at 41b918c9 (io-compression-zip, security-cryptography-random, storage, text-regular-expressions); Storage is linked privately by CNA's storage module.
The full engine has no automatic Windows build or run; only the Win32 platform harness is cross-built and run under Wine, and all MSVC lanes are manual.
GDI's cross-built examples are not registered with CTest in a cross tree; GDI's only automatic CTest route is the manual native workflow.

candidates.section: Windows II: Wine and Engagement Gates
candidates.text: The Direct2D Wine lane has no d2d1 engagement marker and every Direct2D registration bypasses the DXVK gate, so which Direct2D implementation ran is shown only by environment controls.

CnaTests links -sJSPI=1 while, as a CNA-owned executable without CNA_EMSCRIPTEN_ASYNCIFY=OFF, it also receives -sASYNCIFY=1; its comment still describes a -fwasm-exceptions root ABI. Whether the two suspension settings conflict was not established.

candidates.section: Web III: Five Renderers, Four Kinds of Evidence
candidates.text: Only HTML_DOM has an automatic browser run; SVG_DOM's browser runner has no workflow or CTest caller, CANVAS/WEBGL1/WEBGL2 have no browser harness, and WEBGL1 is built by no workflow.

Android has no workflow or preset; the only execution records are emulator runs of an earlier revision with no retained artifacts, and content loading through ContentManager inside an APK is untested.
Mobile lifecycle handling is covered only by a portable test; no device or emulator test drives background, foreground, low memory or process recreation.
iOS evidence is a device final-link and one simulator frame; no physical device run exists, and tvOS/watchOS/visionOS are refused at configure time.
No CNA code resolves an Apple application bundle's Resources directory for content; a relative content root depends on the working directory and SDL's file-open rules, untested for a launched bundle.

candidates.section: Discovery needs a controlled escape hatch
candidates.text: In cross-compiled DIRECTX9, DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12 and Direct2D trees, CnaTests carries a CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR that runs the Wine wrapper with its engagement gate disabled (CNA_D3D9_SKIP_DXVK_GATE=1, CNA_D3D11_SKIP_DXVK_GATE=1, CNA_D3D12_SKIP_VKD3D_GATE=1). The property applies to discovery and to every discovered case and CnaTests-command route (e.g. CnaInputTests), so a GoogleTest case that creates a device in such a tree is not proven to have run through DXVK or vkd3d-proton.
candidates.evidence: cmake/UnitTests.cmake (set_target_properties(CnaTests PROPERTIES CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR ...) and its comment naming CnaInputTests)

candidates.section: Proton solves a different reproducibility problem
candidates.text: The DIRECTX12 Proton lane defaults to the moving "Proton - Experimental" runtime, records no pinned identity, applies no log-token gate and forwards only the child exit status (exec python3 proton run), so a pass through it is not reproducible and does not prove vkd3d-proton served the run; the three DirectX12 Proton fixtures depend on it.

Software_XnaLineCoverage, described by CNA as a permanent exact CTest for the two line scenes, runs run-oracle-corpus-diff-software.sh, which exits non-zero only on a render failure or missing reference; a pixel difference is printed as DIFF and the test still passes.

No workflow runs the XNA oracle corpus: D3D9_XNA_Diff exists only in a DIRECTX9 MinGW tree under Wine+DXVK, Fna3d_XNA_Oracle and the line-coverage CTests are in no workflow configuration except that EasyGL_XnaLineCoverage is reachable from general-tests-ci.yml, which does not install the Pillow module xna-diff.py imports. The DIRECTX9 39/39 record has not been repeated on native Windows.

candidates.section: Can a green test go red?
candidates.text: The Direct2D mutation checker is wired only as --dry-run (anchor existence) in the manual-dispatch d3d-windows-ci.yml; the --run mode that rebuilds and requires each targeted test to fail is never automated, so no mutation is known to be killed.
No workflow configures gcov, lcov, gcovr or llvm-cov and no CMake option adds coverage instrumentation; the only line-coverage figure is a hand-recorded 2026-08-18 report for graphics-ext.

The libFuzzer/AFL-capable harnesses (cna_compiled_effect_fuzzer with CNA_FX_FUZZER_ENTRY_POINT, cna_xna_model_fuzzer, cna_xna_intermediate_fuzzer, and the C API StringView/CubeLut fuzz sources) are not CTests and no workflow runs any fuzzing campaign; only deterministic fuzz-named GoogleTests run.
candidates.evidence: cmake/Harnesses.cmake (fuzzer targets, "Not registered as a ctest"); modules/c-api/tests/fuzz/

candidates.text: The FNA value-differential harness (tools/fna-reference, cna_reference_dump, compare-fna-reference.py) is a manual workflow: not a CTest and not in CI, and its comparison is one-directional (CNA-only keys are never reported).
Recorded Vulkan, Software and DirectX11 glTF L7 golden sets and the registered WebGPU, SDL_GPU and OpenGL4 parity-fixture CTests are run by no workflow; only the EasyGL/OPENGLES3 L7 job is in CI.

No workflow or configure preset enables CNA_BUILD_INSPECTOR, so the 27 InspectorTests never compile in CI; macOS runtime behaviour is recorded by CNA as pending; the WebBridge has no automated test (see B9 P2-102).
